editorial: Every time you think the sky belongs to you, a new shadow looms over the horizon, and Supergirl (2026) turns that notion on its head. The film pairs a star‑powered heroine with a cynical, street‑wise ally whose off‑hand sarcasm feels like a cosmic mixtape, freshening the superhero genre. Director Zadie Smith layers rim‑lit frames and a pulsating synth score, giving every chase a tangible heartbeat that stays with you long after the credits roll. At times the story lurches into a sluggish middle, leaving you wishing the momentum returned sooner. You’ll buy in if you crave a gritty superhero saga that blends high‑stakes action with detective noir twists.
targetAudience: Ideal for those who appreciate high‑octane superhero epics that balance spectacle with cerebral stakes.
